text:
Sam Colangelo is getting another real run with the Ducks after playing just nine NHL games last season. The 24-year-old winger from Stoneham, Massachusetts, a 2020 second-round pick, has five points in 15 games on about 10 and a half minutes a night, and he has been doing the dirty work too, with 31 hits.

The early points came in a burst: four assists in a four-game stretch in late October, including two against Vancouver. Since then the minutes have shrunk, by about two a night over his last ten games. His own shooting looks unlucky, one goal on 2.11 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and the finishing touch he showed before should count for something: Evolving-Hockey had most of his value in 2024-25 coming from even-strength offense, though in only 400 minutes. The concern is what happens around him. Anaheim takes about half the shot attempts at five on five with him on the ice but only 34% of the expected goals, nearly 13 points worse than without him. Fifteen games is a small sample, but that gap is the one that decides whether he keeps a regular spot.
headline: Sam Colangelo's chances are fine, the defense isn't
